messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — novaedge-prod private VPC — elevated 5xx rate and NLB unhealthy targets for tenant novaedge. Trigger: NLB health checks failing (HTTP 502) across 3 AZs. Alert group: network/egress. Pager: @oncall-ryan

oncall-ryan: saw it, jumping in. Can someone confirm customer impact?

support-liam: customer reports increased error rate from their app. They see ~70% 502s for image-generation endpoints. They're on Dedicated pool in private VPC.

sre-ana: checking NLB health in console now. Target group shows 0/12 healthy. Health check logs show `HTTP/1.1 502` from targets.

eng-evan: quick check — were any recent deploys to novaedge-dedicated? Deploy bot shows no deploys in last 24h.

se-jess: no deploys. Last config change was a security group update yesterday but that was outbound-only. Could be stateful conntrack exhaustion or a backend process crash.

sre-ana: running remote curl from inside VPC to backend VIP: ```curl -v http://10.200.45.23/health || true
*   TCP handshake ok, response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

oncall-ryan: can we hit instance directly (bypass NLB) to check app health?

eng-evan: attempting direct IPs of targets (10.200.45.24, .25, .26): responses vary. .24 returns 200, .25 returns timeout, .26 returns 502. Looks like flapping.

sre-ana: checking instance logs — backend process (fastapi) shows repeated upstream timeout to model-worker: `ERROR: upstream request timeout to 127.0.0.1:8081` at scale. Model worker logs show frequent OOM kills around the time errors started.

se-jess: customer is on a dedicated smaller instance class for model-worker. Could be memory pressure due to bigger prompts or cache growth.

support-liam: Customer confirms an internal traffic surge from a scheduled batch. They can throttle if needed but want us to handle without downtime.

oncall-ryan: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily shift traffic away from NLB to a healthy fallback ALB (pre-provisioned), 2) roll model-worker service to larger instance class on the affected nodes, 3) adjust SG/timeouts if needed. Who can own DNS weight shift?

dns-bot: DNS change request received: shift novaedge-prod-weighted record from weight 100 -> 0 to route to fallback pool. Approval required from oncall.

oncall-ryan: approved. Do it. :thumbsup:

dns-bot: starting weighted DNS change. TTL for the record is 60s. Expected propagation within ~2m.

eng-evan: creating traffic-shift CCW: `aws elb modify-listener --load-balancer-name novaedge-nlb --default-actions TargetGroupArn=arn:...,Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=fallback-targets` (dry run). Will coordinate with infra.

sre-ana: meanwhile I'm scaling up model-worker on the affected nodes: `kubectl patch deployment novaedge-modelworker -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"worker","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"16Gi"},"requests":{"memory":"8Gi"}}}]}}}}'`

se-jess: please add a rolling restart after patch: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/novaedge-modelworker` so that new pods pick up resource limits.

eng-evan: ALB fallback already has warm targets in another VPC via VPC peering (configured for DR). I'll flip the DNS weight to 100 for fallback and 0 for primary now.

dns-bot: weight updated. New distribution: fallback=100, primary=0. Monitor: traffic should drop on NLB.

sre-ana: NLB target health improving? Checking... still shows 0/12 healthy but we see decreasing connection attempts. Backend OOM logs continue but frequency dropping after model-worker restart.

support-liam: customer reports errors dropping to ~10% now. They're throttling batch jobs as further safety.

oncall-ryan: good. Keep the fallback for now until we confirm stable. Next steps: (A) confirm model-worker stable (no OOM) for 30m, (B) run a controlled gradual weight back to primary if healthy, (C) document for handoff.

eng-evan: adding a short-lived route for outbound egress via proxy to reduce connection churn: `iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 443 -j REDIRECT --to-port 3128` on the model-worker hosts (applies only to fallback nodes) — will monitor.

sre-ana: observing model-worker memory at 45% after restart (was 92% before). No OOMs in last 8 minutes. Logs show normal request handling.

se-jess: I'm preparing a postmortem note and a runbook update: add autoscaling rule for model-worker memory pressure and a soft throttle for scheduled batch jobs.

oncall-ryan: handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. @sre-ana you'll be primary, @eng-evan on infra, @se-jess on customer comms, @support-liam on customer coordination. Confirm please.

sre-ana: confirmed, taking ownership. I'll keep the fallback weight for 30m and then run a 5-minute ramp back to primary if metrics stable.

eng-evan: infra note — we'll snapshot the affected nodes and open a ticket to upsell novaedge to a higher dedicated tier if they want sustained capacity.

support-liam: informing customer of current state and next steps. ETA for full cutback ~45m-1h.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=sev2, impact=customer-visible errors reduced after DNS failover, mitigation=traffic-shift to fallback ALB + model-worker resource upgrade, next_action=handoff to SRE, runbook_update_required=true

oncall-ryan: thanks team. If anything regresses wake me. :white_check_mark:

sre-ana: will post follow-up summary and timeline in ~45m.

se-jess: adding immediate runbook actions to repo: `docs/runbooks/vpc-private/novaedge-dedicated-memory-throttle.md` (draft).

eng-evan: marking infra tasks: #INC-239001 upgrade nodes, snapshot, validate peering latency.

support-liam: customer acknowledges and appreciates rapid response.

incident-bot: End of thread summary appended to incident ticket INC-239001.
